newsitem.title: FRANCE: Swissair says Paris cargo activity normal.
newsitem.headline: Swissair says Paris cargo activity normal.

text.p: Swissair's cargo activities at Paris-Charles de Gaulle airport are operating normally today following strike action yesterday by staff protesting plans to cut jobs.
"There was some disruption yesterday but we still managed to handle all scheduled shipments while today it's business as usual," a CDG-based Swissair cargo official told Reuters.
The official added: "We don't expect any further action by CDG cargo staff this week but one can't be 100 percent sure given that the dispute is not yet settled."

Swissair and staff representatives were meeting to discuss the airline's French restructuring programme. This involves cutting 66 jobs, including around 25 staff in cargo handling operations, which will be outsourced from January 1, 1997, the official said.
"Swissair will do all it can to transfer as many staff to other posts within the group to minimise redundancies."
Swissair had invited tenders for its cargo handling activties at CDG where the three main operators are France Handling, Societe de Fret et de Services (SFS) and Air France.
At Lyon-Satolas airport, Swissair is to continue self-handling services for cargo, the official added.

At Marseille and Nice airports, where Swissair is represented by agents Aerocargo International, cargo handling is outsourced to the Air France group. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
